quote: No. This is Debbie. It's wife.
stewart_read: Wrong-contact scenario — rep is speaking to the spouse of the actual lead, not the lead himself.
coaching_implication: Rep should immediately clarify whether Mike is reachable now or schedule a specific callback with him, rather than running the pitch on Debbie.

quote: Well, I just I just saw the estimator. I was just looking at it.
stewart_read: This is the interest question moment and it reveals near-zero intent; the rep skips interest_question per verified events and never probes this disclosure.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged probing pointless since Debbie isn't the lead — but that doesn't justify pitching the bill swap moments later.
coaching_implication: Should have asked a clarifying follow-up ('so is Mike the one looking into this, or is this something you're both curious about?') before pitching anything.

quote: but I wasn't particularly interested. But I was just like, okay. What does it cost?
stewart_read: Second explicit disclaimer of interest; rep does not acknowledge it and instead offers to build a design.
coaching_implication: Repeated disinterest statements should trigger a scope check — confirm who the real decision-maker is before investing further pitch time.

quote: Yeah. And then you know about the bill swap too?
stewart_read: Rep launches into explaining the bill swap financial mechanism unprompted, closer-tier content, before any verify items are captured.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be a strategic hook to create curiosity — but it's delivered as a feature explanation, not a question that pulls her in, and no bill amount was ever captured to anchor it to.
coaching_implication: Redirect financial-mechanism explanations to the specialist call; use the hook only after establishing genuine buyer identity and bill pain.

quote: Please just send my husband email, and and we'll go from there.
stewart_read: Debbie hands the rep a direct path to the real decision-maker (email) and the rep doesn't capture it, offering to text her instead.
coaching_implication: This is the single biggest miss on the call — capture the husband's email or a callback window for him instead of substituting a text to the wrong contact.

quote: I can hear. I can just text you, and you can always have my number. And if you want Okay. Text me back, you can.
stewart_read: Call ends with no date, no time, no confirmed next step — just an offer to text the wrong contact.
coaching_implication: Should have asked for the husband's contact directly or set a specific callback time to reach him.
